leftEvidence.title: Jesus compares lilies with Solomon’s glory

points.label: Solomon-relative action
points.left: Jesus points to lilies clothed by God and says Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of them.
points.right: Jesus directs disciples from anxiety to ravens and lilies, saying Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one flower.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Anxious hearers are directed from royal splendor to ordinary creation and divine care.
points.right: Hearers are called to seek God’s Kingdom rather than live by anxious pursuit.

payload.posture: Both Gospels preserve Solomon as the lesser comparison to flowers clothed by God within teaching about anxiety.

rightEvidence.title: Luke remembers Solomon’s glory among the lilies

payload.tension: Shared saying material remains embedded in distinct Gospel sequences and audiences.
payload.title: Solomon and the lilies in Matthew and Luke
